why_zero_qpu: a completed IBM job is re-fetchable, so the first hardware reading of this instrument costs nothing. Scoring is not a device act
weight_model: device calibration snapshot; weights are log((1-p)/p)

certified_weight.physical_reading: a proven lower bound on the negative log-probability of the error that actually occurred
certified_weight.claim: every shot's minimum-weight explanation lies in its own [lower, upper]; the lower end is a proven bound on the weight of the error that actually occurred, and holds for refused shots too because weak duality needs feasibility, not optimality
certified_weight.does_not_claim: a physical error RATE. These are weights under the declared detector error model. A wrong model makes this a certified interval about the wrong graph -- see oneq.dem_calibration

notes.population_bound_method: percentile bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 20260831 -- distribution-free, because per-shot weights are right-skewed and a normal interval is worst exactly there
notes.why_every_shot: refused shots carry a valid lower bound (weak duality needs feasibility, not optimality) and are the HARD shots; excluding them would make the measurement improve whenever the decoder got worse

soft_estimate.out_of_range_means: s = (-1)^L lies in [-1, 1] by definition. A value outside it is not a measurement of s: it proves the reliabilities are wrong -- most often a gap clamp that understates confidence, so the debias over-corrects
soft_estimate.claim: the minimum-variance linear estimator of the logical value, weighting each shot by its calibrated complementary gap
soft_estimate.does_not_claim: (a) unbiasedness when the calibration curve DIFFERS between the two logical values -- see parity_calibration_split; that bias does not shrink with more shots. (b) a gain against CURRENT PRACTICE. The multiplier compares against equal weighting of the SAME debiased terms, which nobody actually does; a majority vote is biased, so comparing to it needs mean-squared error rather than variance and is a different measurement

notes.why_two_rates: the debias wants an unbiased rate -- too low and it overshoots, which is how a clamped model produced +1.3033 on hardware. The weights want a rate that cannot be optimistic, because overstated confidence understates every error bar downstream

soft_estimate_from_MODEL_confidence.out_of_range_means: s = (-1)^L lies in [-1, 1] by definition. A value outside it is not a measurement of s: it proves the reliabilities are wrong -- most often a gap clamp that understates confidence, so the debias over-corrects
soft_estimate_from_MODEL_confidence.claim: the minimum-variance linear estimator of the logical value, weighting each shot by its calibrated complementary gap
soft_estimate_from_MODEL_confidence.does_not_claim: (a) unbiasedness when the calibration curve DIFFERS between the two logical values -- see parity_calibration_split; that bias does not shrink with more shots. (b) a gain against CURRENT PRACTICE. The multiplier compares against equal weighting of the SAME debiased terms, which nobody actually does; a majority vote is biased, so comparing to it needs mean-squared error rather than variance and is a different measurement

notes.why_clamp: beyond the gap where calibration has power, p = 1/(1+e^g) is an extrapolation; weighting by it produced a measured 49,881x multiplier that no evidence supported

why_two_estimates: the measured estimate weights by confidence the shots actually demonstrated; the model estimate weights by 1/(1+e^gap). Where they disagree, the model is claiming confidence the data does not carry -- and an |s| > 1 on either is proof its reliabilities are wrong, since (-1)^L cannot leave [-1, 1]

parity_calibration_split.why: the weighted estimator assumes one calibration curve serves both logical values; where these two columns diverge, one reliability cannot debias both and the resulting bias does not shrink with more shots

dem_calibration.verdict: significant but immaterial: real, and smaller than 0.02
dem_calibration.claim: whether the declared detector error model predicts its own misprediction rate, measured against device outcomes through the decoder's posterior geometry
dem_calibration.does_not_claim: which mechanism is wrong. A miscalibration says the model and the device disagree and in which direction, not which edge weight to change

notes.why_power: a bin expecting 0.003 errors is consistent with the model and with one ten times worse; shots are not power, and a verdict from a powerless bin reads the same whether the model is right or untested
notes.why_two_bars: a chi-square on a million shots rejects a deviation in the fourth decimal, and on four hundred rejects nothing; significance and size answer different questions and both are required

lag1.claim: an EXACT test: under i.i.d. shot order is exchangeable, so permuting the observed values gives the null distribution with no distributional assumption at all
lag1.does_not_claim: that the device is stable when p is large. It claims only that no effect ABOVE the stated sensitivity was found; a smaller one would have been invisible

notes.why_exact: shot order is exchangeable under i.i.d., so the permutation null needs no model

block_scan.no_combined_p_value: these share one dataset and are strongly correlated, so agreement between them is close to guaranteed and a combined p-value computed as though they were independent would overstate the evidence badly
block_scan.how_to_read: one block size clearing its own bar is a finding; four of them leaning the same way without clearing it is a hint that a larger sample could settle

exchangeability.why: an EXACT test of the assumption every DEM rests on. Under i.i.d. shot order carries no information, so permuting the observed syndrome weights gives the null outright -- no distributional family to be wrong about. A large p here means only that nothing ABOVE the reported sensitivity was found

does_not_claim: on --dry-run, ANYTHING about a device: the shots are sampled from the same edge model that decodes them, which is the circularity DO-1 is declared a proxy for. On --refetch the shots are the device's and the model is the device's published calibration, so neither generated the other -- but the calibration is a SNAPSHOT and the job is one session
